statusReason: Goldman Sachs provides a dated US power-demand and on-time activation forecast, while Bloomberg Law and Reuters report Project Jupiter force-majeure and loan-pricing observations. Contract text, facility-level energized MW, final debt terms, independent corroboration, production visuals, and publication remain outstanding.

marketForecastReadback.boundary: Goldman Sachs Research forecast based on scheduled capacity and utilization assumptions; it does not prove any individual site's energized MW, COD, or loss.

verifiedClaims: Bloomberg Law reports that Oracle sent a force-majeure notice to a Blue Owl unit regarding Project Jupiter.
The report describes payment deferral protection if the project fails to come online in 2028 as planned.
entries.boundary: People familiar with the matter are cited; the contract, notice text, and final outcome are not publicly verified here.

verifiedClaims: Reuters reports that approximately US$18 billion of loans tied to an Oracle-leased New Mexico data center were quoted at 89–91 cents on the dollar by syndicate banks including Santander and Jefferies.
entries.boundary: The quoted loan price is a reported market observation and does not establish a realized loss, default, or final lender exposure.

interpretationBoundaries: Planned MW, power secured, grid connected, construction complete, and energized MW are separate states.
A force-majeure notice is not proof of termination, default, or realized loss.
A loan quote below par is not the same as a realized impairment or lender loss.
Goldman Sachs forecast percentages must not be presented as facility-level production results.
The loss-propagation diagram is a conditional mechanism, not an investment recommendation.
